descripcion: At C1, idioms of mid frequency are expected in discussion and comment, not the textbook ones nobody actually says. The rule matters as much as the list: one idiom per paragraph, never two in a row, and always checked against register before use.

filas: to cut a long story short

ejemplos.texto: To cut a long story short, they sent us to a different office entirely.
We spent three weeks going round in circles with no real progress.
As a last resort, we escalated it to management.

notas: Idioms are almost never varied in wording; playing with them usually reads as an error rather than wit when a learner does it.
Check register before using an idiom: to be a nightmare is fine with a colleague and wrong in a formal letter.
Three idioms in one paragraph sounds like a phrasebook, not a person — one is plenty.

es.en: Idiom images rarely match: no tener pelos en la lengua has no English version with hair (the equivalent is not mince words). Literal translation almost never works, so each idiom is best learned as a unit.
es.es: Las imágenes de los modismos rara vez coinciden: «no tener pelos en la lengua» no tiene un equivalente inglés con pelos; el equivalente es «not mince words». La traducción literal casi nunca funciona, por lo que cada modismo conviene aprenderlo como una unidad.

de.en: Some Germanic images match (der Apfel fällt nicht weit vom Stamm – the apple doesn't fall far from the tree), but many only half-match (die Katze im Sack kaufen – buy a pig in a poke). The half-matches are the most misleading.
de.de: Einige germanische Bilder stimmen überein («der Apfel fällt nicht weit vom Stamm» – «the apple doesn't fall far from the tree»), viele passen aber nur halb («die Katze im Sack kaufen» – «buy a pig in a poke»). Gerade diese halben Übereinstimmungen sind am irreführendsten.

it.en: Idiom images rarely match (in bocca al lupo – break a leg), so literal translation almost never works. Each idiom is best learned as a unit.
it.it: Le immagini idiomatiche corrispondono raramente («in bocca al lupo» – «break a leg»), quindi la traduzione letterale quasi mai funziona. Ogni idiom va imparato come un'unità.

fr.en: Idiom images rarely match (poser un lapin – stand someone up), so literal translation almost never works. Each idiom is best learned as a unit.
fr.fr: Les images idiomatiques correspondent rarement («poser un lapin» – «stand someone up»), donc la traduction littérale fonctionne presque jamais. Chaque idiome doit s'apprendre comme une unité.

pt.en: Some images are close but not identical (custar os olhos da cara – cost an arm and a leg), which makes literal translation tempting but wrong. Each idiom is best learned as a unit.
pt.pt: Algumas imagens são próximas, mas não idênticas («custar os olhos da cara» – «cost an arm and a leg»), o que torna a tradução literal tentadora, porém errada. Cada idiom deve ser aprendido como uma unidade.

errores: Translating an idiom from your own language word for word into English.
Using an informal idiom in a formal written context.
Stacking more than one idiom in the same paragraph.

redemittel.expresion: One idiom per paragraph is plenty.
redemittel.funcion: states the usage rule the skill asks for

traducciones.es: Con un modismo por párrafo alcanza.
traducciones.it: Un modo di dire per paragrafo basta.

autochequeo: Is there at most one idiom per paragraph?
Does each idiom fit the register of the surrounding text?
Is any idiom a literal translation from Spanish?
Is the wording of each idiom kept fixed, not varied?
Would a native speaker actually use this idiom in this context?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the idioms used. Check the wording, the register and whether any idiom reads as a literal translation from Spanish. Flag more than one idiom per paragraph. Do not rewrite the text.

es: «*meter la pata*» rendered as *put the paw in* instead of *put your foot in it*.
de: *Tomaten auf den Augen haben* rendered as *have tomatoes on your eyes* instead of *be blind to something*.
it: «*avere le mani bucate*» rendered as *have holed hands* instead of *spend money like water*.
fr: *avoir le cafard* rendered as *have the cockroach* instead of *feel down*.
pt: *estar com a pulga atrás da orelha* rendered as *have a flea behind the ear* instead of *smell a rat*.
